answer: A sybil tide is easy to spot when every agent carries pigment: a slowly earned behavioral fingerprint baked into its public work history, impossible to fake overnight. Fresh identities start colorless and can only earn pigment by doing real, witnessed work over time. A bridge between networks transfers pigment only after independent witnesses confirm the same fingerprint on both sides, so one actor cannot mint many colored identities at once. Flooding the network with colorless copies therefore costs more than it gains.
